clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by mutations in HK1 (hexokinase 1), historically described as hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy Russe type (HMSN-Russe or HMSNR).
A founder disorder classically identified in Roma populations, with the causative change lying in a nerve-specific alternative 5' untranslated region of HK1 rather than in the coding sequence.
Onset in childhood to early adolescence with distal lower-limb weakness and wasting that later spreads to the hands.
Prominent distal sensory loss develops, and severe distal muscle atrophy can cause substantial disability by adulthood.
Electrophysiology shows an intermediate to slowed conduction pattern, faster than classic demyelinating CMT1 yet slowed relative to pure axonal forms.
Consider the diagnosis specifically in a consanguineous family or one of Roma ancestry with recessive CMT.
Diagnosis depends on identifying biallelic HK1 regulatory-region variants; analysis limited to the standard coding exons may miss the founder change.
It shares a population background with CMT4D (NDRG1, HMSN-Lom), another Roma founder neuropathy.
reference.pathophysiology: CMT4G is caused by mutations in HK1, which encodes hexokinase 1, the enzyme catalysing the first committed step of glycolysis by phosphorylating glucose to glucose-6-phosphate. The disease-associated founder change lies not in the ubiquitously expressed coding region but within an alternatively spliced, nerve-specific untranslated first exon that governs a neural HK1 transcript. The mutation is thought to disrupt regulation and expression of this isoform in peripheral nerve, impairing local glucose metabolism and energy supply in Schwann cells and axons. The result is a slowly progressive neuropathy with intermediate electrophysiology, reflecting combined effects on myelination and axonal integrity rather than a purely demyelinating or purely axonal process.
additionalDifferentials: Other autosomal recessive demyelinating CMT4 subtypes (CMT4A GDAP1, CMT4C SH3TC2)
CMT4D (NDRG1, HMSN-Lom), another Roma founder disorder
Acquired chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy as a treatable mimic
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography, expecting intermediate to slowed values
Gene panel or exome sequencing including HK1 with explicit coverage of the nerve-specific untranslated exon
Assessment of ancestry and consanguinity, with targeted founder-variant testing where appropriate
Family segregation and parental carrier testing
Nerve imaging, or rarely nerve biopsy, if the diagnosis remains unclear
Clinical genetics referral and genetic counselling
redFlags: Rapid deterioration or a relapsing course suggesting superimposed inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy
Marked asymmetry or conduction block on nerve conduction studies, which is atypical for inherited disease
Early severe respiratory or bulbar involvement
reference.prognosis: CMT4G is slowly but steadily progressive; distal weakness and sensory loss can cause substantial disability and loss of independent ambulation in some patients by mid-adulthood, although life expectancy is not typically shortened.
pitfalls: Screening only the HK1 coding exons and missing the founder variant in the untranslated regulatory exon.
Overlooking the diagnosis outside the classically described population when consanguinity is present.
Mislabelling the intermediate conduction pattern as either pure CMT1 or pure CMT2.
Failing to consider treatable inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy in an atypical or rapidly progressive presentation.
management: No disease-specific pharmacotherapy; supportive and rehabilitative care through a neuromuscular multidisciplinary team
Physiotherapy, stretching and ankle-foot orthoses for distal lower-limb weakness and foot drop
Occupational and hand therapy with adaptive aids as the hands and severe distal wasting develop
Podiatry and orthopaedic care for foot deformity
Neuropathic pain management with gabapentinoids or tricyclic agents for prominent distal sensory loss
Avoidance of neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine
Autosomal recessive genetic counselling with founder-variant (HK1) testing and family screening, guided by Roma ancestry and consanguinity
